title: Actionable Insights from Observational Data: The Case of Advanced Classes in K-12 Education
abstract: arXiv:2609.23836v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A fundamentally challenging question in K-12 education is about the effects of taking more advanced or challenging classes. It is particularly complex because students (and/or their parents) choose whether to enroll in these classes, making causal analysis challenging. In this paper, we begin to tackle this question by taking advantage of a novel dataset from a public school system in the US. This dataset records students' course enrollment decisions, prior academic histories, demographics, and subsequent outcomes around the time of a district-wide change that introduced optional open-enrollment advanced middle-school courses in subject areas. This is a rich observational dataset, but enrollment in advanced classes is driven by student characteristics and choices rather than random assignment. translated_title: 从观测数据中获得可行动的洞察：K-12教育中高级课程的案例
translated_abstract: K-12教育中一个根本性的难题是：修读更多高级或更具挑战性的课程会产生何种效果。这个问题尤为复杂，因为学生（和/或其家长）自行决定是否选修这些课程，使得因果分析充满挑战。在本文中，我们利用来自美国一个公立学校系统的新颖数据集开始着手解决这一问题。该数据集记录了在一个学区范围内按学科引入可选的开放式注册初中高级课程这一变革前后，学生的课程选修决策、过往学业记录、人口统计特征以及随后的结果。这是一个丰富的观测数据集，但高级课程的选修是由学生特征和选择所驱动，而非随机分配。这带来了一个核心的识别挑战：影响高级课程选修的相同因素同样能够预测学业结果……
tldr: 本文利用美国某公立学区引入开放式注册初中高级课程这一政策变革前后的新颖观测数据，研究学生选修高级课程对学业结果的因果效应，并应对学生自选择带来的识别难题。
en_tdlr: This paper leverages a novel observational dataset from a US public school district around a policy change introducing open-enrollment advanced middle-school courses to study the causal effects of taking advanced classes on academic outcomes, tackling the identification challenge posed by student self-selection.
